new_finding: Let H=X†X be PSD in any fixed product basis. If its offdiagonal support graph G is connected and has a vertex with at least three neighbours, the compound modulus R=|H^[2]| strictly overestimates S2(X)=λmax(H^[2]), regardless of all complex edge phases. In the two-token support graph take a branch center o and neighbours a,b,c. Its six configurations {o,a}→{a,b}→{o,b}→{b,c}→{o,c}→{a,c}→{o,a} form a cycle whose compound-edge product is −|h_oa h_ob h_oc|², so it is always phase-unbalanced. The two-token graph of a connected G is connected: fix a leaf of a spanning tree, move the token nearest that leaf there without collision, and configurations with one token at the leaf are connected by moving the other in the remaining tree.
